newsitem.title: DJIBOUTI: Djibouti proposes pension should ruler step down.
newsitem.headline: Djibouti proposes pension should ruler step down.

text.p: The Djibouti Council of Ministers has proposed granting President Hassan Gouled Aptidon, ruler since 1977, a pension should he step down.

The bill, proposed on Sunday, would allow the Council "the terms of granting former presidents of the republic a pension," under Article 39 of the constitution. It could only apply to Gouled who has ruled since independence.
Political analysts said the bill could pave the way for Gouled, in his early 80s, to step down in 1999 at the end of his present six-year term, though legally he could seek another term.
Gouled collapsed with a lung infection at a Francophone summit in Cotonou, Benin in 1995. He was treated in France and returned to Djibouti in March 1996.
Djibouti is one of the world's poorest countries and in May asked donors for $87 million in aid to revive the largely barren nation at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
